rank_one_coefficient_curve.singularity_type: three real ordinary nodes; no cusps
rank_one_coefficient_curve.no_cusp_certificate: dx/dt0=3t0^2-2 and dy/dt0=2t0(2t0^2-3) have no common zero
rank_one_coefficient_curve.interpretation: the equation detects the compact rank-one Sym3(SU2) coefficient image; generic USp4 Haar is not supported on it, but the equation alone does not certify arithmetic Sym3 origin over F_q

odd_q_arithmetic_false_positive.arithmetic_obstruction: an elliptic source over F_q would need an integer trace t with t^2=2q; for odd q, v_2(2q)=1, so 2q is not a square
odd_q_arithmetic_false_positive.conclusion: membership in the compact coefficient curve is not sufficient even for local arithmetic symmetric-cube recognition

odd_q_arithmetic_lattice_avoidance.theorem: for every odd integer q, t -> t^3-2qt is injective on integer t; hence the Sym3 trace alone recovers the base Frobenius trace

mod_4_certificate.conclusion: the second factor cannot vanish for distinct integers

odd_q_arithmetic_lattice_avoidance.oddness_is_load_bearing: at q=2, t=0 and t=2 both have Sym3 trace 0
odd_q_arithmetic_lattice_avoidance.geometric_meaning: the real coefficient parameterization folds and has nodes, but the odd-q restriction places no two integral traces in the same trace fiber; one arithmetic branch may still share a value with a nonarithmetic real branch
